text.text_excerpt: This place is a lot like the Diagon Alley of unpretentious eats. You'd never know it was there unless you worked in the area, and even then, I've found that not many people I meet have heard of it or have even seen it when they pass by on the street. Seems like a weird way to turn a profit, but if it works for the owners, who am I to comment? Bottom line is that Louisiana Products is a great place to stop in for a hot plate or a sandwich, and it also has a nice selection of snacks and drinks to tide you over. Prices are extremely reasonable - I've walked out of there with a soda, sandwich, and fresh baked chocolate chip cookies for under $6 - and the people who run the place are very nice...

We need a consolidation of the two pages for Louisiana Products! But onto the substance: I don't want the hidden-gem aspect of the place to be trounced by an influx of visitors, but since we're such good friends, I'll let you in on the joy of Louisiana Products. Just promise me you won't take the last plate of red beans and rice on Monday and we're cool. Run by the two sweetest ladies you've ever met, this a true blue community favorite where you can slip in and become a regular right-quick. A can of soda's sixty cents. Did you move to New Orleans after Katrina and heard stories about the way things used to be? Well, to the best of my understanding, this little gem of a place is one of the last of its kind. Frozen in time, staffed by genuinely delightful people, this deli provides joy and sustenance at least once or twice a week. My favorite is the oven fried pork chops, mashed potatoes and gravy, and mustard greens - a must have on Thursday. Add some coconut pecan cookies and you're all set. But don't take it with you - eat there and make new friends. And while you're there, you will see for sale behind the counter something that you've been looking for but haven't seen in awhile.
